clue.text: Cast takes on a hunt

parts.note: to cast metal is to forge it

explanation.surface: A theatre company signs up for a hunt, perhaps a treasure hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' wants to be the actors; here it is the verb from metalwork. The A slips in after FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: animals search for food by rummaging about, and the noun works the same way, a forage being a hunt.

clue.text: Italian director collapsed in current

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A film director collapses into a river or the flow of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: Federico Fellini made La Dolce Vita. I for current comes from physics formulae.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the maker of La Dolce Vita and 8½ is one of the best-known filmmakers Italy produced.

clue.text: Sauces made using spun sugar

indicators.note: spun letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook makes sauces from spun sugar, as for candyfloss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun sugar' is a real confectioner's term, which hides the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the slow-cooked Bolognese meat sauce is one kind of sauce, pluralised to match.

clue.text: Speculated about how visitor is picked up

indicators.note: what is picked up is heard, so the answer is how the word is heard

parts.note: a visitor is a guest, and that word said aloud is a past-tense verb spelt differently

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a caller might be collected from the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as fetching a visitor by car; it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: forming an opinion without firm evidence.

clue.text: Music system created by some austere orchestras

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

parts.note: drop AU from the front and keep only the O of the second word

explanation.surface: A sound system is designed by a few severe orchestras.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the end of 'austere' plus the O of 'orchestras'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a two-channel system for playing music.

clue.text: Cheers advanced facility

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A pub toast, followed by a new state-of-the-art building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building; it is the other sense, a knack. Ta and cheers are both casual British thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of natural ability: a facility with numbers is a gift for them.

clue.text: Way to seek admission that will sound familiar

definitions.note: the first definition is a noun phrase; ring a bell is the action it names
definitions.meaning: you ring the doorbell to be let in
a name that rings a bell is one you seem to know

explanation.surface: A tip on how to get into a house that the reader will half recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is a nudge toward the bell itself, which makes the two senses meet neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing the bell is how you ask to come in; something that rings a bell sounds familiar.

clue.text: Published fiction on queen is something abnormal

parts.note: a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A newly released novel about a queen is judged strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Published fiction' reads as one thing, a novel, but it splits in two. Queen as R is from the Latin regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a data point or thing far from the norm.

clue.text: Mostly what you wear and feel in battle

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase; the answer is the condition felt

indicators.note: most of the phrase is kept: the last letter goes

parts.note: the camouflage uniform soldiers wear, a plural name

explanation.surface: A description of the soldier's uniform and the strain felt in war.
explanation.walkthrough: The clothing and the condition share a name, one letter apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat fatigue is the exhaustion and stress soldiers suffer in battle.

clue.text: Promote extremely punctual underling

indicators.note: take only the extremes, the first and last letters, of each word

explanation.surface: A boss rewards a very reliable junior with a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely punctual' reads as very punctual; 'extremely' covers both words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: an author on a chat show mentions a new book to push sales.

clue.text: Texan lopes about finding places out of this world

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cowboy ambles around and stumbles on somewhere otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' usually means wonderful; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoplanets are planets outside our solar system.

clue.text: Casually called wife the most beautiful in America

parts.note: the beauty-contest winner holds the title Miss

explanation.surface: A husband calls his wife the loveliest woman in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss US would be the country's beauty queen. Missus is informal British for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The missus is a casual word for one's wife.

clue.text: Biblical fellow creating difficulty in African country

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

explanation.surface: A man from the Bible stirs up trouble on a trip to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' only links; Benin is the small West African country beside Nigeria, and the difficulty goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son in Genesis.

clue.text: Sad fitter abandoned initial romantic encounter

indicators.note: abandoned as in wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A gloomy tradesman walked out of a first romantic meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as walking out on the date; it signals letters without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: initial matches the ordinal, and a romantic encounter arranged in advance is a date.

clue.text: Being in good form accurately underpins race odds

indicators.note: in a down answer, what underpins goes below

parts.note: SP = starting price, the odds at the off

explanation.surface: A racing tipster whose accurate form reading supports the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good form' sounds like racing form, the horse's record; it means lively. SP is the betting term for the starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy.

clue.text: You express absolute resolution when starting this time

indicators.note: take each word at its start, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: New Year talk: this time I mean it, says the resolution-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a New Year's resolution, and the answer is the year it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The year is the period the resolution is meant to cover.

clue.text: Fossil fuel that may lead to war?

definitions.meaning: peat, cut in blocks from bogs and burnt on the fire
a word that goes before 'war' for a fight between gangs over territory

explanation.surface: A remark that burning fossil fuels might end in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a word that comes before 'war': a turf war. Turf is peat, the fuel dug from bogs in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is peat for burning, and it goes before 'war' in turf war.

clue.text: Wedges have this fine finish — it's just the start

definitions.meaning: a wedge tapers to a narrow edge at one end
from the idiom for a small first step that will lead to much worse

explanation.surface: A remark about wedges' neat edge, plus a warning of more to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the thin end of the wedge' names a small first step toward something bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge ends thinly, and the thin end of the wedge is only the start.

clue.text: Unrivalled competition? Not so much

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the rivalry is unbeatable and is told: not really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrivalled competition' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Unrivalled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal.

clue.text: Reluctantly deliver expression of horror to disrupt power grab

indicators.note: the word breaks into the other and splits it

explanation.surface: A reluctant messenger's cry of dismay helps foil an attempted takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: UGH breaks COUP into CO and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To cough up is to hand over money or information unwillingly.

clue.text: Devotee of major pop sensation broke wifi set

indicators.note: broken letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An excited fan of a big pop star crashes the wifi setup.
explanation.walkthrough: The pop sensation is Taylor Swift, whose fans are called Swifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiftie is a devoted fan of Taylor Swift.

clue.text: Boiled rice in iron container — that's very intense

indicators.note: boiled letters are stirred into a new order
the rearranged letters go in the other piece

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Rice boiled in an iron pot turns out scorching hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container' is part of the kitchen picture; the pot that holds the rice is FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: heat, competition or loyalty described this way is at full strength.

clue.text: Fish sounding very small to contribute food for Italians

parts.note: the ling is a sea fish

indicators.note: the answer is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: weeny = tiny; run on after the fish, it gives the rest of the sound

explanation.surface: A tiny fish plays its part in an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: LING + WEENY, said together, gives the pasta's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a flat Italian pasta.

clue.text: Media snubs insider's return — it's not reported

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words
the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: The press ignores a whistleblower's comeback, so the story goes untold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insider' reads as a whistleblower; it points to letters inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something left unspoken has not been told to anyone.

clue.text: Informed about liberal jargon

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: an informer sings to the police

explanation.surface: Someone told on a liberal over their use of jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing, so the past tense SANG = informed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both name the vocabulary a particular group uses in place of standard words.

clue.text: Don't be fooled by this flimsy type of material

definitions.meaning: to detect a trick or a liar's real motive
sheer fabric, thin enough to show what is behind it

explanation.surface: A warning not to be taken in by a cheap, thin fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase and the adjective are spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: You see through a deception; sheer fabric is see-through.

clue.text: Pretentious faction loses power

indicators.note: a group that loses something no longer has it, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a political party is a faction

explanation.surface: A political splinter group, full of airs, is voted out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY without its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means showily artistic, pretentious.

clue.text: Really dull study of poet

parts.note: dry = very dull, as in dry as dust
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: A critic calls an academic study of a poet deadly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as a piece of scholarship; it is the room. John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was England's first Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Top primate nursing bruised ego

indicators.note: bruised letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The alpha ape comforts a rival whose pride has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top primate' reads as the alpha ape; 'Top' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest point, a peak.
